name: MonarchTheme
title: ToggleGroup
wrapsNative: A Row of selectable MonarchChips for any number pressed; MonarchSegmentedControl (Modifier.selectable with the radio button role) for at most one
summary: Related toggle buttons in one row, with any number pressed or at most one: selectable MonarchChips or a MonarchSegmentedControl.
whenToUse: For two to five related options that are each on or off, such as Bold, Italic and Underline, or an optional single choice that can be released, such as a text alignment.
whenNotToUse: For a required single choice that switches views, use the single-choice segmented buttons as in SegmentedControl. For one on or off option use a toggle button or MonarchSwitchRow. For filters with many options use MonarchTag.
api: @Composable fun MonarchChip(text: String, selected: Boolean, onSelectedChange: (Boolean) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, size: MonarchTagSize = MonarchTagSize.Md, enabled: Boolean = true, leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, selectedIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchSegmentedControl(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, size: MonarchSegmentedControlSize = MonarchSegmentedControlSize.Md, fillWidth: Boolean = false, content: @Composable MonarchSegmentedControlScope.() -> Unit)

@Composable fun MonarchSegmentedControlScope.Segment(selected: Boolean, onClick: () -> Unit, label: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, count: Int? = null, suffix: String? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)

options.name: checked
options.description: Multi-choice (MonarchChip selected): whether this item is pressed. State is hoisted: the app keeps the set of pressed items.

options.name: onSelectedChange
options.description: Multi-choice (MonarchChip): called with the new state of this item.

options.name: selected
options.description: Single choice (Segment): whether this item is the pressed one.

options.name: onClick
options.description: Single choice (Segment): called when the item is pressed. To let the pressed item be released (the web's single type without required), store null when the pressed item is pressed again.

options.name: size
options.description: The height of the segments (Sm, Md, Lg) or of the chips (Sm, Md); the touch target stays 48dp.

options.name: icon
options.description: An icon before the label: icon on Segment, leadingIcon on MonarchChip. There is no check mark.

options.name: label
options.description: The option's text, with a count when needed (Segment has count, a chip puts it in the text).

options.name: modifier (row)
options.description: Give the row a name with Modifier.semantics { contentDescription = "Text style" }, as the web requires an aria-label.

states.name: pressed
states.description: Chip: the accent tint with accent text and an accent border. Segment: the raised indicator under the item.

states.name: not pressed
states.description: Chip: a hairline border and no fill. Segment: the muted track.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The disabled text color; taps are ignored.

appearance: Pressed chips take the accent tint, accent text and an accent border; the segmented control is a muted track with one raised indicator (the surface with a hairline in light themes, one surface step up in dark ones) that slides to the chosen item. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ToggleGroup is a row of separate toggle buttons with one Tab stop, arrow keys, Home and End, a loop option, variants, sizes and icon-only items; iOS ships a MonarchToggleGroup wrapper. On Android Monarch ships no type: any number pressed is a row of selectable MonarchChips (spaced, each with its selected state), and at most one is a MonarchSegmentedControl (the RadioButton role and selection, one raised indicator), each with a 48dp target. Keyboard focus moves item by item, as in every Compose row; the web's roving tab stop and loop are not offered. The web's single type without required (pressing the pressed item releases it) is written by the app in onClick, as the example shows. The chips are 28dp (24dp small) and the segmented control has Sm, Md and Lg. An icon-only segment uses the icon slot with a content description. The web's default and outline variants are not offered.
accessibility: Chips expose a selected state, read as selected or not selected; segments have the RadioButton role and are selected or not selected.
A pressed chip changes fill, text and border together, and the chosen segment is the raised one, so the state is not color alone.
Every item reserves a touch target of at least 48dp by 48dp.
A disabled item is read as disabled and ignores taps.
Items follow the layout direction, and labels are not cut at font scale 2.0 in a short row.
The row is named by the app with a content description.
edgeCases: Segments share the row width when it is filled; keep labels to one or two words. Chips wrap to the next line in a FlowRow.
More than five options become too narrow for a segmented control on a phone; use chips instead.
